Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree so you don't collide with parallel work happening on this same repo right now:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir -b feature/freemc-public main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir`, symlink node_modules from the primary tree if it's not already usable (`ls node_modules` — if missing/broken: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`), and symlink the env: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env` if `.env` isn't present. Do ALL your work in this worktree, not in /opt/nxeon directly.

This worktree already has a 12-mode "free Minecraft server" product on main (commit c2e97e9): one free Docker-based Minecraft server per account on a shared host behind itzg/mc-router (subdomain-based routing, e.g. `myworld.play.nxeon.cloud`).

READ FIRST: `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` (for `FREEMC_PRESETS`, `getFreeServerStatus`/`getFreeServerPlayers` status helpers), `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `FreeMinecraftServer` model (already has the fields you need: `isPublic Boolean @default(false)`, `publicTagline String?`, `publicDescription String?`, plus `subdomain`, `name`, `preset`, `status`), and `app/(marketing)/free-minecraft/page.tsx` (the existing marketing page for this product — copy its metadata/OG/JSON-LD/hero patterns exactly for consistency; it also shows the established SEO conventions in this codebase). Also read `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx`'s `Manage` component for the existing card/form visual style you should match.

YOUR TASK — build an opt-in public server directory: server owners can make their free server publicly joinable and listed, with its own shareable marketing page.

1. `lib/actions-freemc-public.ts` — `"use server"`: `updateFreeMinecraftPublicListing(prev, formData)`: `requireUser()`, load caller's `FreeMinecraftServer`, read `isPublic` (checkbox), `publicTagline` (trim, cap ~80 chars), `publicDescription` (trim, cap ~600 chars, strip/escape — this will be rendered as plain text on a public page, never as raw HTML, so no need to sanitize HTML but do trim and length-cap), update the row. No container/SSH changes needed — purely a DB update gating what's shown publicly.

2. `components/customer/freemc/PublicListingCard.tsx` — `"use client"`, a self-contained card (matching the existing `Manage` tab's card style: `card max-w-md space-y-3` etc. from `FreeMcDashboard.tsx`) with the toggle + tagline + description fields + save button, and — when `isPublic` is on — a "View your public page" link to `/servers/{subdomain}`. This component is meant to be dropped into the existing Manage tab later by someone else; it must NOT edit `FreeMcDashboard.tsx` itself and should accept `server: { subdomain: string; isPublic: boolean; publicTagline: string | null; publicDescription: string | null }` as a prop.

3. `app/(marketing)/servers/page.tsx` — directory listing every `isPublic: true, status: "READY"` `FreeMinecraftServer`, newest first, capped at a sane page size (~48) — no pagination needed for v1, just cap and note the cap rather than silently truncating without saying so in a comment. Each card: display name (`name ?? subdomain`), tagline, the game mode's label+description (via `FREEMC_PRESETS[preset]`), connect address (`{subdomain}.{domain}` — fetch the domain the same way the existing dashboard page does: `getSetting("free_minecraft_domain", "play.nxeon.cloud")`). Live player counts are a nice-to-have, not required for v1 — if you include them, do it in a way that can't make the page slow or fail if freemc-host is briefly unreachable (e.g. best-effort with a short per-server timeout, or skip live counts server-side entirely and note that as a deliberate choice). Full SEO metadata (`generateMetadata`, OG tags) matching the `/free-minecraft` page's pattern.

4. `app/(marketing)/servers/[subdomain]/page.tsx` — the individual server's own public page. MUST call Next's `notFound()` (404) if the server doesn't exist, OR `isPublic` is false, OR `status !== "READY"` — this is a hard security/privacy requirement: a private server's existence or address must never be inferable from this route, not even via response-time or error-message differences beyond a plain 404. Show: display name, tagline, description, mode label+description, connect address with a copy affordance, live status if you can get it cheaply (optional). Full `generateMetadata` (title from server name, description from tagline, OG image — reuse `/games/art/minecraft_hero.jpg` if reusing the existing hero asset makes sense, check what image assets already exist for the Minecraft product under `public/games/art/` or similar).

5. SEO/sitemap: find how this codebase already generates its sitemap (search for `sitemap` — likely `app/sitemap.ts` or `app/sitemap.xml/route.ts`, and check whether there's an existing per-entity dynamic sitemap pattern, e.g. how blog posts are included, if a blog exists in this codebase). Add the static `/servers` directory page as a sitemap entry. For the dynamic `/servers/[subdomain]` pages: follow whatever pattern the codebase already uses for other dynamic/per-entity pages if one exists (query `isPublic:true, status:"READY"` rows and include each); if no such dynamic-sitemap pattern exists anywhere in the codebase, use your judgment on whether it's worth adding one now vs. just shipping the static `/servers` entry — document your decision either way in your final report, don't silently skip it.

6. Do NOT edit `FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, `actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, or any other existing file except the sitemap file (which you should edit carefully, additively — read it fully first, don't remove anything already there). Do NOT merge to main or push anywhere. Do NOT delete your worktree when done — I'll integrate from it and clean it up myself.

7. Before finishing: `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` in your worktree must both pass clean. Commit your work in the worktree (git add the new/edited files explicitly, never `git add -A`) so it's not lost.

Report back: the file paths created/edited, your sitemap decision and why, the worktree path/branch name, and confirmation the build/typecheck passed.

1	/**
2	 * Docker/RCON control primitives for free-tier Minecraft containers on
3	 * freemc-host — the free-tier equivalent of lib/game-control.ts, which speaks
4	 * to full Proxmox-VM game servers over SSH+tunnelled RCON. This is much
5	 * simpler: one SSH hop to the host, then `docker exec <container> ...` for
6	 * everything, using the CLI tools itzg/docker-minecraft-server already bundles
7	 * (rcon-cli, mc-monitor) instead of a hand-rolled RCON protocol client.
8	 *
9	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from both lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
10	 * and, in future, a worker sweep, same reasoning as lib/game-control.ts.
11	 */
12	import { scryptSync } from "node:crypto";
13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
15	
16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}
28	
29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}
33	
34	export type ServerStatus = {
35	  running: boolean;
36	  players: { online: number; max: number } | null;
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
52	    return { running: false, players: null };
53	  }
54	  const status = await dockerExec(
55	    conn,
56	    containerName,
57	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
58	    10_000,
59	  );
60	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
61	  try {
62	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);
63	    const p = parsed?.server_info?.players;
64	    if (typeof p?.online === "number" && typeof p?.max === "number") {
65	      return { running: true, players: { online: p.online, max: p.max } };
66	    }
67	  } catch {
68	    /* fall through */
69	  }
70	  return { running: true, players: null };
71	}
72	
73	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
74	
75	/** One RCON round-trip via the bundled rcon-cli — see lib/game-control.ts's
76	 *  validateRconCommand for the same input sanitation used on the paid path. */
77	export async function sendRcon(
78	  conn: Client,
79	  containerName: string,
80	  ownerId: string,
81	  command: string,
82	): Promise<RconResult> {
83	  const password = rconPasswordFor(ownerId);
84	  const r = await dockerExec(
85	    conn,
86	    containerName,
87	    `env RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(password)} rcon-cli ${shellQuote(command)}`,
88	    12_000,
89	  );
90	  if (r.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: r.stderr.trim() || "RCON command failed." };

98	  conn: Client,
99	  containerName: string,
100	  ownerId: string,
101	): Promise<{ ok: true; players: PlayerInfo[] } | { ok: false; error: string }> {
102	  const r = await sendRcon(conn, containerName, ownerId, "list");
103	  if (!r.ok) return r;
104	  const colonIdx = r.response.indexOf(":");
105	  if (colonIdx === -1) return { ok: true, players: [] };
106	  const names = r.response
107	    .slice(colonIdx + 1)
108	    .split(",")
109	    .map((s) => s.trim())

114	/** Reads /data/server.properties into a plain key->value map. */
115	export async function readServerProperties(
116	  conn: Client,
117	  containerName: string,
118	): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
119	  const r = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, "cat /data/server.properties", 10_000);
120	  if (r.code !== 0) return {};
121	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
122	  for (const line of r.stdout.split("\n")) {
123	    if (!line || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
124	    const i = line.indexOf("=");
125	    if (i === -1) continue;
126	    out[line.slice(0, i).trim()] = line.slice(i + 1).trim();
127	  }
128	  return out;

134	 * itzg entrypoint's normal boot sequence picks the new values up — the image
135	 * only reads server.properties at startup (confirmed against the Minecraft
136	 * wiki: none of gamemode/motd/max-players/etc. persist a live RCON change back
137	 * to the file), so a restart is the only fully-reliable way to apply anything
138	 * here. Keys with a real live RCON equivalent (difficulty, whitelist on/off)
139	 * are ALSO pushed live by the caller for instant effect — see FIELD_LIVE_CMD.

142	  conn: Client,
143	  containerName: string,
144	  changes: Record<string, string>,
145	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
146	  const current = await readServerProperties(conn, containerName);
147	  const merged = { ...current, ...changes };
148	  const body = Object.entries(merged)
149	    .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`)

152	    conn,
153	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c 'cat > /data/server.properties'`,
154	    body + "\n",

## Summary

**Worktree:** `/opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir`, branch `feature/freemc-public`, commit `6840947`. Not merged, not pushed, not deleted — left in place for integration.

**Files created:**
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir/lib/actions-freemc-public.ts` — `"use server"` action `updateFreeMinecraftPublicListing`: `requireUser()` + rate limit, loads the caller's row, trims/caps `publicTagline` (80 chars) and `publicDescription` (600 chars), updates `isPublic`/`publicTagline`/`publicDescription`. Pure DB write, no SSH/container touch.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir/components/customer/freemc/PublicListingCard.tsx` — self-contained `"use client"` card matching the `Manage` tab's `card max-w-md space-y-3` style, with toggle/tagline/description/save, and a "View your public page" link when `isPublic`. Not wired into `FreeMcDashboard.tsx` — that's a deliberate follow-up left for whoever integrates it, per your instructions not to edit that file.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir/components/customer/freemc/ConnectAddressCopy.tsx` — small client-only copy-to-clipboard component, split out because the server page needs `generateMetadata`/`notFound()` and can't itself be `"use client"`.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir/app/(marketing)/servers/page.tsx` — directory of `isPublic:true, status:"READY"` servers, newest first, capped at 48 (documented in-code as a deliberate v1 cap, not silent truncation). Live player counts deliberately **omitted server-side** here — documented in a comment: doing per-listing SSH lookups on an unauthenticated page for up to 48 servers risked hanging the whole directory if freemc-host is slow/unreachable. Full metadata/OG matching `/free-minecraft`'s pattern.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir/app/(marketing)/servers/[subdomain]/page.tsx` — individual server page. Hard `notFound()` unless the row exists AND `isPublic` AND `status === "READY"` (same gate used identically in `generateMetadata` and the page body, so they can't disagree). `force-dynamic` so a server made private is never served stale. Live status here IS included, but bounded by a manual 4s `Promise.race` timeout wrapped in try/catch (best-effort, never blocks/fails the page) — a tighter bound than relying on `withServerSsh`'s own 15s connect timeout, since this is a single lookup rather than N.

**File edited:** `/opt/nxeon-wt-pubdir/app/sitemap.ts` — additive only. Added the static `/servers` entry, and a dynamic per-server sitemap block that queries `isPublic:true, status:"READY"` rows, mirroring the existing blog-post pattern exactly (same defensive try/catch shape). Nothing removed.

**Sitemap decision:** the codebase already has one dynamic-sitemap precedent (blog posts, gated defensively with try/catch), so I followed it rather than skipping — added a per-server entry for every public+READY row, uncapped (unlike the directory page's 48-cap), since a sitemap is allowed to list more than a single listing page displays.

**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` passed clean; `npm run build` completed with exit code 0, and the build output confirms both `/servers` and `/servers/[subdomain]` compiled as dynamic (`ƒ`) routes alongside the rest of the app.

**Git hygiene:** staged and committed only the new/edited files by explicit path (`app/sitemap.ts`, the two new `app/(marketing)/servers/...` pages, the two new components, and the new lib file) — never `git add -A`, so the `node_modules` symlink in this worktree stayed untracked and out of the commit, per the known worktree hazard.
